title: Each of the 12 merge-queue runs that failed in the last 18 has a verdict from its log, and the causes that recur are fixed at their cause
description: Serves "Nothing breaks the viewers' evening.". Each failed run delays the dogfood's redeploy. After the cutover (JS-194), a failure in a check JS-194 removed gets no verdict. 12 of the last 18 merge-queue runs failed (lead, 2026-11-22), nearly every one on a different test; one shard process hit its 45-minute timeout. Each costs about 45 minutes and a requeue, and delays the dogfood's redeploy. Whether any is a product race is unverified. Same shape as JS-155 (D-042). D-058.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/testing.md gains a JS-175 table of exactly these 12 failed merge_group runs of CI, the full runs (integration tier run, not a plan-only run) of the 18 that ended before the brief of 2026-11-22 19:29 CST: 44983050791, 44986442604, 44989897226, 44994615953, 44997492843, 45008394219 (PR 246 at 45fa298), 45017053835 (PR 247 at 30af59c), 45041377896, 45045804305 (PR 249), 45049599358 (PR 250), 45076662687 (PR 247 at 39bede1), 45086436037 (PR 251). One row per failing test or subtest that the run's gotestsum summary lists as FAIL, a test stopped by the 45-minute timeout included (30 rows: 13 of them in 45017053835, 2 each in 44997492843, 45008394219, 45041377896, 45049599358, 45076662687 and 45086436037, 1 in each other run), each with the run id, the PR and the commit queued, the job (`integration shard (i of 4)` or `(rest)`) and, where the log says it, the go test process (`process k/n`), the test's full name, its first error line as file:line and message, and one verdict. A verdict is one of: (a) a cause owned by a task, naming it and the record or decision that states it: JS-158 (the kit's TRUNCATE deadlock), JS-159 (a cut-short segment stored), one of JS-160's three, JS-171 (the port taken between pick and bind, or the seek checks' 180 s margin), JS-172 (the flood check's at-rest comparison, or the lead's forced carry-over precondition), JS-173 (the refusal after a give-up); (b) the queued PR's own defect, fixed before that PR merged: the row names the escape line in .results/tasks.jsonl and the commit or run after which the test passed; such a row is not a failure of main and counts toward no test cause of criterion 3; (c) a new named cause, with the log line or forced run it rests on; (d) cause unknown, saying what the log lacks. A sighting whose cause is not in its log and is not reproduced is (d), never a test verdict (D-042). The table also carries, in the same form, the failed or cancelled queue runs from the brief to the first run counted by criterion 7 (as of 2026-11-23 23:00Z: 45132952457 cancelled, 45135324010, 45177074145, 45186563932), so no failure falls between the two windows. Beneath it, counts per cause, by row and by run (a run counted once under each cause any of its rows has), and how many of the 12 runs had a row in neither (a) nor (b), so the table says whether the 12 are one cause or many. The record is not read by any test. (D-074) For the 12 runs, a row whose cause a merged task owns, or that was the queued PR's own defect, carries only the run id, the test's name and the verdict. A row not read is marked so and is read in full if its test fails a counted run.

For every verdict that is the product's, the row says what a viewer and what an operator would have seen in production (a freeze, a refusal and its dialog, a stall and for how long, extra reads, a log line or nothing), from the log or the code it cites, marking what is unverified. JS-159's two rows and JS-173's one carry the viewer effect their records give and need no new brief. Each other product verdict returns to the product owner as a brief before any product fix, and nothing in the product (any non-test file outside docs/ and tasks/) is changed by this task. Among them the record gives a verdict, with its evidence, for at least: the copied job in 45041377896 (`TestEveryJobOfEveryWorkerGoesOnThroughAnOutage/switchover`) whose ffmpeg reached the film's end while the worker's loop waited at the fence for an unanswered renewal and logged `ffmpeg cannot be paused here, so this job runs without a lead limit` (whether invariant 57's lead holds while the fence waits); the restart past the first segment not stored in 45135324010 and 45186563932 (`TestALivenessURLThatRefusesEveryWorkerForLongerThanALeaseCancelsEveryJobAndTheNextRequestRestartsIt`, liveness_url_integration_test.go:454, `job 7 restarted its spec at segment 5` and `at segment 3`; the second run carried no JS-161 code); and the viewer answered 503 after 15.5 s behind the transaction-mode pooler in 45017053835 (`TestALivenessURLBehindATransactionModePoolerEitherNamesTheFlagOrLeavesTheKilledWorkersJobToItsLease`, liveness_url_pooler_integration_test.go:266 and :278), which may be JS-168's first build's own defect.

A new test cause seen in two or more runs is fixed at its cause in the test kit. Before the fix its condition is forced once, with real processes or real contention, and the test is seen to fail as the queue's log shows; after the fix the same forcing passes. The procedure and both results are recorded in docs/testing.md; no test of the kit is committed (D-069). A cause seen once, or one whose condition cannot be forced, is recorded as unknown and left.

Reproduction is bounded: only for a sighting whose verdict may be the product's (criterion 2): at most 2 hours of wall-clock runs each and 4 hours in all (D-074), under CI's shape (`test/ffmpeg61.sh`, ffmpeg 6.1, 2 CPUs pinned with `JELLYSCALE_TEST_CPUS` that no other run uses, a fresh Postgres each run). Rows whose verdict is (a) or (b) need no reproduction. The record gives, for each sighting tried, the command, the runs made, the failures and their messages, and the hours spent, and the total; a sighting left when its box ran out keeps verdict (d).

The shard that hit 45 minutes is named with its healthy time over the 18 runs and what it was running when stopped. After the behaviour-only cleanup merges, test/shard-times.txt is regenerated from three successful merge-queue runs, so every dealt test has a measured time, and the four shards' healthy times are recorded. If a shard's healthy time is then still within 10 minutes of the timeout, it is split as internal/transcode is split, with no test dropped (closes BL-175); eight shards are not adopted otherwise. The record gives the time each of JS-172's flood tests adds to it. (D-069) The 10-minute rule is applied to the measured healthy time of the next three successful queue runs (35.1 minutes predicted on 2026-11-24): at 35 minutes or more that process is split (D-074).

TestAHeldWorkerEndsAJobWaitingForItsSubtitleTrackBeforeItsLeaseRunsOut is counted apart in criterion 7's 10 runs, as ran and failed; a failure that is the refusal JS-173 removed (`cores are short ... most any worker has free is 0.0` right after a give-up) returns JS-173 to the product owner as a brief (D-074).

After JS-158 (merged, cb1a65c) and this task merge, the next 10 merge_group runs of CI that run the integration tier (a plan-only run that skips it is not counted), starting with the first queued after d7dbeeb (PR 279), are counted in docs/testing.md: each run's id, PR and conclusion, and for each failed run every failed job and test with its first error line and a verdict as in criterion 1. The count of failed runs of 10 and the causes come to the product owner at that triage, with whether more than 2 failed (D-058, D-063: JS-160's place). The two cut-read recovery cases are counted apart in those 10 runs, each as ran and failed: the waiting-request case (the three `TestAFailureThatIsNotTheFilesIsMadeAgainForTheRequestThatWaited/<a re-encode | a copy | a job that burns in a subtitle>, the source store cuts a read` subtests) and the persisting-cause case (`TestACauseThatPersistsStartsAtMostThreeFreshJobsAndThenFails/the source store cuts a read`); one failure of either returns JS-159 to the product owner as a brief. Each counted run's log, and for a failed job its tests.json and failures.log, is searched for `40P01`: one outside the tests that provoke it on purpose (TestADeadlockOrSerializationFailureOnAWorkersWriteNeverFailsTheJob, TestASegmentCommitThatPostgresAbortsForADeadlockNeverFailsTheJob) is listed, and one on a job end (`recording the end of a transcode job failed`) promotes BL-260 (D-063). The record says that a passing test's output is not printed, so a `40P01` inside one is not seen. No hook is added to the worker to force the exit-first order (D-061). Each failure also says whether it is load: Postgres or a store that did not answer within the test's bound on the runner, the test passing alone under CI's shape. Two or more bring one test process per shard job to the product owner as a priced brief. The runs of PRs 270, 277 and 279 on 2026-11-24 are reported apart (D-074).

No retry, no skip, no raised timeout (go test's 45m in test/integration.sh, the seek checks' 180 s, any wait of a test or the kit) and no widened bound: no test's bound is raised, the rig's lease is not lengthened, and no check is amended to pass. No product code is changed to fit a test, and none is changed at all by this task (criterion 1's verdicts are written, not built). No viewer-visible change. Regenerating test/shard-times.txt decides only the deal of tests to shards and is not a bound (D-069).
notes: ux: false, core: false. Reads JS-158's and JS-159's records when they exist; waits for neither. Does not hold any merge (owner, 2026-11-21). Runs beside JS-161; its reproduction runs do not share a machine with JS-174's measurement. If criterion 1 shows one cause behind most of the 12, the lead brings that count back before criteria 3 to 5 are built, and the task is cut to that cause. D-069: the table and the 10-run count also say, for each failure, whether it was a defect of the change itself that the integration shards on the pull request (ci:full) would have shown, and whether it was the fault-schedule test on a random seed. Columns of the table, not new work. Three or more of the first in the 10 runs brings integration shards on every code pull request to the product owner as a criterion of JS-097; one of the second on a build later shown right brings the fixed-seed list back as a brief. D-074: merges in parts, as PR 277 did; closes when the 10 runs are counted. A pull request that adds or changes integration tests runs ci:full once before it is queued.
